sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 5.4% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, but the path was a commodity cycle rather than a trend [F177].
Revenue fell 32.5% in FY2020 to $94.5 billion, then rose 64.7% in FY2021 and 51.5% in FY2022 to $236 billion [F5][F6][F7][D153][D192][D232].
The FY2022 increase was primarily driven by higher upstream realizations and downstream margins [P57].
Revenue then declined in each of FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, to $184 billion, a 7.9% three-year CAGR [F8][F9][F10][D626].
Chevron U.S.A. Inc. supplied 75.1% of FY2025 revenue and subtracted 3.9pp from growth as it fell 5.3% [D402][D403][D404].
Tengizchevroil was the offset, at 11.6% of revenue and +1.5pp, growing 16.5% [D418][D419][D420].
FY2025 sales fell mainly on lower crude oil and refined product prices, partly offset by higher volumes and natural gas prices [P17].
Operating costs grew 1.2pp faster than revenue in FY2025, at -3.4% against -4.6% [D373][D379][D358].
Net income fell 30.5% while diluted EPS fell 31.8% as the diluted share count rose 2.1% [D359][D361][D374].
Net margin of 6.7% in FY2025 sat below the 7.9% window median and far below the 15.1% FY2022 high [F30][D613][D612].
Cost of revenue fell to 57.2% of revenue from 58.8%, while SG&A rose to 2.7% from 2.4% [D338][D296][D340][D298].
Depreciation, depletion and amortization rose to 10.7% of revenue on higher production and higher rates [D341][P12].
The 36.8% effective tax rate left net margin 2.5pp below the prior year, a 2.5pp decline [D345][D369].
Operating cash flow of $33.9 billion was 2.76x net income, above the 1.97x window median [F60][D346][D644].
The FY2025 increase came primarily from higher cash distributions from TCO and legacy Hess assets more than offsetting lower commodity prices [P6].
Free cash flow of $16.6 billion was a 8.8% margin, below the 8.9% window median and the 13.4% peer median [F80][D343][D616][D634].
Capex of $17.3 billion was 9.2% of revenue and 0.86x D&A [F70][D342][D348].
Cash and investments were $7.3 billion at FY2025 against $11.4 billion of debt issued in the year [D349][X157].
Total assets jumped 26.1% to $324 billion and equity 22.4% to $186 billion, consistent with the Hess acquisition [F110][F176][D365][D367].
Buybacks and dividends of $24.8 billion were 149.7% of free cash flow, above the FY2022 level of 59.1% [D353][D354][D228].
Return on average equity of 7.3% was below the 14.9% peer median [D357][D642].
Revenue declined for three straight years, FY2023 through FY2025 [R1][F8][F9][F10].
The decline reflects commodity prices rather than lost volume, since production rose 12% in FY2025 [P28].
Buybacks and dividends exceeded free cash flow in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 [R4][D270][D312][D354].
Payout above free cash flow is being funded by balance-sheet capacity and asset sales, which is not durable indefinitely.
Revenue for FY2018 through FY2025 in the table is a later recast, not the figure first reported, so growth and margins mix two presentations [R3][F10][X10].
Comparisons spanning the recast years should be read with that basis break in mind.
Whether FY2026 revenue falls below the FY2025 level of $184 billion, in the FY2026 10-K [F10].
Whether free cash flow margin recovers above the 8.9% window median, in the FY2026 10-K [D616].
Whether buybacks and dividends fall below 149.7% of free cash flow, in the FY2026 10-K [D354].
